## Summary

Ruckus began in 2002 as an incubator project and was incorporated in 2004 as Video54 Technologies by William Kish and Victor Shtrom; it is headquartered in Sunnyvale, California, and makes Wi-Fi access points, CBRS access points, switches, controllers and management software, with the BeamFlex adaptive directional antenna as its signature technology [1]. Brocade bought it in 2016, ARRIS bought the Ruckus and ICX businesses in 2017, CommScope acquired ARRIS in 2019, and Belden agreed on 30 April 2026 to buy Ruckus, a purchase announced complete on 1 July 2026 [1]. The IEEE registry lists 99 MA-L blocks to "Ruckus Wireless" at 350 West Java Drive, Sunnyvale [2].

A MAC in these blocks is most likely an enterprise access point, bridge or ICX switch [1][4]. WikiDevi documents an Atheros AR7161 with AR9223 and AR9220 radios in the ZoneFlex 7363, a Qualcomm Atheros QCA9557 with QCA9882 in the outdoor ZoneFlex T300, and a Qualcomm IPQ8074A with QCN5124 and QCN5154 802.11ax radios in the R730 and R750; the M510 carries an LTE modem [4]. Ruckus FCC IDs start with S9G, with U2M on two ZoneFlex models [3][4].

In December 2019 a researcher reported several vulnerabilities in the web interface of a number of Ruckus routers, which the company patched [1]. Randomization behaviour is not documented by the sources consulted; the FCC ID databases refused automated access from this session.
